Beállítom Viktor Orbán’s former press advisor Fanny Kaminski has spoken up after the Prime Minister’s Office, led by Bálint Ruff had filed a complaint relating to the contracts about Viktor Orbán’s social media accounts. The complaint was filed against an unknown perpetrator after reviewing the former prime minister’s most recent contracts with her company relating to managing his social media profiles, which came to a total of 4 billion forints (around €11 million) in public funds over several years. Kaminski, whose company was awarded the contract without a public procurement process, wrote on Facebook that her company, Triton Communications, had carried out all tasks assigned to it under the contract and could provide a detailed account of the work performed. According to her, the government has made several insinuations concerning the matter, which paint a misleading picture of their work, so she would like to set the record straight on a few facts. She wrote that Triton Communications’ contractual obligations didn’t merely consist of taking photographs and videos. The company developed and operated the Prime Minister’s website and also provided graphic design and other communication services. She added that being on call 24/7 was also part of the contract. According to her, this didn't mean occasional tasks, but rather constantly being on standby and reacting straight away when needed. Kaminski confirmed that the payment increased over the four years, but she said the government failed to mention that this was to keep pace with inflation. She further argued that it is also misleading to emphasize that Triton Communications only had five full-time employees, because the work actually involved more than 30 people in total. Fanny Kaminski accepts that the new government is reviewing its predecessor’s contracts. “However, I refuse to accept that in the process, they are trying to cast suspicion on a law-abiding Hungarian company by using cherry-picked figures, omitting facts, and using misleading insinuations,” she stated. As a postscript, she added: “I’m proud to be among the first to be dragged through the mud. Photo: Zane Bitere/LETA “Are we going to shoot down every drone with fighter jets from now on? If that’s the case, then it’s over – we’re in serious trouble,” MEP Ivars Ijabs, deputy chairman of the board of the For Latvia’s Development party, said on TV24 programme Runāsim atklāti! (“Let’s Speak Openly!”). Speaking about Latvia’s security and defence, one of the current issues is tunnels dug by migrants. According to independent MP of the 14th Saeima and reserve colonel of the National Armed Forces (NBS) Igors Rajevs, the tunnels being discovered along the border are a new phenomenon in Latvia, although they are nothing new or surprising in other countries. “Poland had such tunnels two or three years ago,” he said. “The Border Guard is working there and monitoring the situation, and let’s be honest – it wasn’t Minister Dombrava who found that tunnel! These things cannot be handled as one-off campaigns; there must be systematic action. It is clear that the new government wants to demonstrate results quickly, which explains all this activity.” To safeguard national security, MP of the 14th Saeima, former Defence Minister and candidate in the 15th Saeima elections Andris Sprūds (PRO) stresses that many measures have already been implemented, including the construction of a border fence, although, as he himself acknowledges, “the fence is not a panacea – what matters most is how institutions coordinate with one another.” “One of the important solutions that must be implemented as quickly as possible – and which was started but has nevertheless encountered some difficulties – is the installation of sensors so that we are technologically capable of responding when a border violation occurs.” Asked by the programme host whether there is really as long a waiting list for procuring sensors as there is for air defence systems, Sprūds replied that the issue involves more than sensors alone. “We are talking about 450 kilometres. Obviously, cables also have to be installed. Yes, years have passed, but first the fence had to be built. I think the previous government faced problems, and this government and the next one will face them as well for as long as the pressure continues. There will be no single silver bullet that solves everything.” Continuing the discussion on security, the participants turned to the issue of drones. Sprūds and Rajevs said that although Latvia has interceptor drones, drones are currently being shot down only by NATO fighter jets. “All drones that have been shot down so far were taken down by NATO fighter jets, not by counter-drone systems,” Rajevs explained. Ijabs expressed concern about this approach: “Is the idea really that from now on we are basically going to shoot down every drone with fighter jets? If that’s the case, then it’s over – we’re in serious trouble.” Meanwhile, Jānis Urbanovičs, chairman of the board of the Harmony party and a candidate in the 15th Saeima elections, recalled events in Rēzekne in May this year, when a drone crashed. “Those drones were flying there and – bang! – they fell. First one came down, then another, but we were told there was only one. Fine, we can’t shoot them all down, but perhaps we could at least detect them?” Read also: BNN IN FOCUS | “How to hit the leader?” Political scientist explains Latvia’s pre-election battle within the coalition Follow us on Facebook and X ! https://www.digi24.ro/stiri/externe/demo.text: Democraţii din Senat i-au cerut lui Elon Musk, directorul general al SpaceX, să păstreze toate documentele legate de restricţionarea serviciului Starlink/Starshield în Ucraina, a relatat Wall Street Journal (WSJ), citând o scrisoare la care a avut acces publicaţia. Solicitarea vine într-un moment în care Ucraina se confruntă din nou cu perturbări semnificative ale sistemului vital de comunicaţii militare. Restricţiile limitează viteza de operare a sistemului Starshield la 161 de kilometri pe oră (100 de mile pe oră), limitând astfel capacitatea Ucrainei de a intercepta dronele de atac ruseşti. Scrisoarea îi solicită lui Musk să păstreze toată documentaţia referitoare la întreruperile serviciului din perioada 13-24 octombrie şi, din nou, din 12 noiembrie, relatează WSJ. „Restricţiile din octombrie şi noiembrie ridică acum posibilitatea îngrijorătoare ca aceste vulnerabilităţi să persiste chiar şi în cadrul sistemelor pe care se bazează guvernul SUA”, au scris senatorii Jeanne Shaheen şi Chris Coons. Senatorii solicită companiei SpaceX să pună la dispoziţie înregistrările începând cu 1 septembrie, inclusiv orice comunicări legate de serviciile Starlink şi Starshield din Ucraina, precum şi comunicările dintre Musk, reprezentanţii SpaceX, Casa Albă şi Departamentul Apărării al SUA. Shaheen şi Coons afirmă că interferenţa cu serviciul Starlink din Ucraina „ridică semne de întrebare serioase cu privire la controlul pe care îl exercită SpaceX” asupra chestiunilor de securitate naţională. De asemenea, aceştia denunţă „procesul decizional opac” al companiei. Scrisoarea îi impune companiei SpaceX să confirme respectarea cerinţelor parlamentarilor şi să răspundă la solicitările de supraveghere până la 30 noiembrie. În declaraţiile făcute presei, SpaceX a negat informaţiile preşedintelui Volodimir Zelenski privind reinstituirea limitelor de viteză. „Este o informaţie falsă. Nu a avut loc nicio schimbare”, a declarat compania pentru Axios. După întreruperea prelungită a serviciului Starshield din octombrie, Musk a susţinut că nu era responsabil pentru decizia de a restricţiona serviciul în Ucraina — în ciuda informaţiilor conform cărora Musk i-ar fi propus planul preşedintelui SUA, Donald Trump, care exercita presiuni asupra Kievului pentru a suspenda atacurile asupra rafinăriilor de petrol ruseşti. Musk a susţinut apoi că Ucraina a încălcat termenii şi condiţiile de utilizare ale Starlink, o acuzaţie pe care Kievul a negat-o. În urma victoriei zdrobitoare obţinute la alegerile intermediare din SUA de la începutul lunii noiembrie, democraţii din Congres intenţionează să lanseze, în ianuarie 2027, o anchetă privind modul în care Casa Albă a gestionat războiul din Ucraina — precum şi implicarea lui Musk.
